attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. 'He' is Satya Nadella, named in the sentence before.

semantics.note: An unhedged factual allegation that Nadella misled investors about how concentrated Microsoft's AI revenue is. The normalised proposition matches it.

contract.note: Zitron names no statement, period or revenue measure. The choice of the April–June 2026 quarter is the evaluator's and narrow, since the allegation may target earlier remarks such as the ARR figure. Requiring an identifiable misleading representation is a fair, ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Secondary summary of a Bloomberg estimate (about 70%). It sets a realized annual figure beside an annualized one and identifies no misleading Nadella statement.
Company transcript. Nadella labelled the $37B figure as ARR, an annualized measure from the prior quarter. On its face this is not a misstatement of concentration.
Shows Microsoft disclosed OpenAI revenue in its July annual report, before the post. This weakens a nondisclosure reading but settles nothing on concentration.
CFO Hood separated out OpenAI in bookings and RPO figures. That is disclosure on a different measure, made by Hood rather than Nadella.

reviews.rationale: The packet identifies no Nadella communication that materially misstated OpenAI's share of AI revenue, and it has no matched numerator and denominator on one basis. Microsoft's disclosures (e3, e4) cut against the claim but do not show that concentration was accurately conveyed. The evidence does not settle it either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence. The 'it won't matter that' framing still asserts the embedded facts as true.

semantics.note: Two present-tense assertions: Anthropic is as unprofitable as OpenAI, and it has made hundreds of billions in promises it can't keep. The comparison with OpenAI is correctly inferred from context.

contract.note: Reading 'just as unprofitable' as similarly loss-making, 'hundreds of billions' as at least $200B, and 'can't keep' as financial inability are ordinary readings. Using Q2 2026 is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 shows $265.6B in fixed commitments, meeting the scale. It shows a large Q2 net loss but positive operating income, and gives no OpenAI comparison and no evidence of inability to pay.

reviews.rationale: Only the scale of commitments is established ($265.6B is at least $200B). The packet has no comparable OpenAI results to test 'just as unprofitable', and the measures conflict (net loss vs operating income). Nothing shows Anthropic cannot meet its commitments. The claim as a whole is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: A claim that $60B annualized revenue by about Nov 18 is necessary for OpenAI to compete with Anthropic. In context, competing means keeping pace with Anthropic's revenue, which was reported at $65B.

contract.note: Reading 'compete' as merely remaining a substantial commercial rival stretches the claim against the speaker. That makes contradiction near-automatic, while his context is revenue parity with Anthropic. Marking the condition 'met' rests on that reading.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 names OpenAI as a primary competitor. That bears on the antecedent, not on whether the threshold was reached by the deadline.
Anonymous-source report of about $50B run rate at end of September. This is an interim figure before the deadline and cannot show a miss.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (about Nov 18, 2026) falls after the evaluation date, and no conclusive event is in the packet. A September run rate below $60B does not establish failure. The claim is not yet scorable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own inference from the quoted Dow Jones/WSJ description. The quoted block itself is not his claim.

semantics.note: The exact sentence asserts only that the guarantee applies once the data center is built. The added 'not to OpenAI's lease payments' comes from the quoted report and a nearby sentence, so the proposition overreaches slightly.

contract.note: Reading the guarantee as operative on completed or service-ready facilities, phase by phase, is fair and ordinary. Treating the lease contrast as residual-value protection rather than routine rent is reasonable.

evidence.note: Reports that the guarantee covers completed data centers, not facilities under construction. This directly matches the claim.

NVIDIA's 10-Q says the guarantees are subject to ready-for-service conditions and grow as each facility enters service. It also ties exposure to defined lease and power payments, which qualifies the added lease-payment wording.

reviews.rationale: Both the reporting and NVIDIA's own filing say the guarantee becomes operative only as facilities are completed and enter service, which is what Zitron's sentence says. The filing does link the guarantee to defined lease and power payments, so the drafter's broader 'not lease payments' gloss is overstated. That gloss is not in the speaker's sentence, and the contract's contradiction condition is not met.
